final_note: You mapped the three legs of the triangle trade and saw why merchants made huge profits.

concepts.def: Trader who buys and sells goods
Items made in factories like guns, cloth
Crops like sugar, tobacco and cotton
Money made after costs are paid

walkthroughs.body_html:
British ships set off from ports like Bristol, Liverpool and London.

They carried manufactured goods — guns, gunpowder, cloth, iron bars, beads and brandy.

On the West African coast (in modern Ghana, Nigeria and Senegal), captains traded these goods with African rulers and slave dealers for captured Africans. 🏴

This was the Middle Passage, the horrific journey across the Atlantic.

Captives were packed below deck in tiny spaces, chained together. The voyage took 6 to 12 weeks. Disease, suicide and brutal punishment killed many.

Survivors were sold at slave markets in the Caribbean, Brazil and the American colonies.

The ships now headed home — but not empty.

They carried raw materials grown by enslaved people: sugar, tobacco, cotton, coffee and rum.

Back in Britain these were sold for huge profits. Some money paid for new manufactured goods, ready for the triangle to begin again. 💷
